title: WebSocket, SSE & Realtime
description: Security controls for persistent connections and browser messaging channels.

attacks.name: WS message fuzzing
attacks.desc: Untrusted WebSocket messages may reach application logic without the same validation used for HTTP requests.
attacks.prevention: Validate every WebSocket message against a schema and apply authorization to the action it requests.

attacks.name: WS missing origin check
attacks.desc: A missing WebSocket Origin check can allow another website to initiate an authenticated connection.
attacks.prevention: Check the WebSocket Origin against an explicit allowlist and require an authenticated handshake.

attacks.name: WS auth on connect only
attacks.desc: Checking a token only at connection time can leave an open channel active after revocation or permission changes.
attacks.prevention: Revalidate permissions for sensitive WebSocket actions and close sessions after token revocation or expiry.

attacks.name: WS smuggling
attacks.desc: Disagreement about WebSocket frame boundaries may let payload bytes bypass intermediary inspection.

attacks.name: WS no rate limit
attacks.desc: Unlimited WebSocket messages can exhaust resources or amplify an application operation.

attacks.name: SSE injection
attacks.desc: Unescaped content in an SSE stream can change how a client interprets event fields.

attacks.name: SSE auth bypass
attacks.desc: An unauthenticated SSE subscription can expose events intended for a particular user or tenant.

attacks.name: BroadcastChannel leakage
attacks.desc: BroadcastChannel messages can expose sensitive state to another same-origin page or tab.

attacks.name: SharedWorker abuse
attacks.desc: SharedWorker state can leak across same-origin contexts when message recipients are not isolated.
